rules.surface_condition: markers immediately before causal/subordinating introducers (surface tokens that typically start clauses that can overturn the preceding span)
rules.blamed_rule: - Is the token immediately after the marker a determiner/preposition/auxiliary/relative pronoun? If yes, bias score downward.
rules.proposed_rule: Scoring rule (downgrade causal/subordinator starts): If the token immediately after the marker is a causal/subordinating introducer (examples: because, causing, due), apply a strong downward adjustment so the marker falls in a low band (suggested target band: 10–35). Rationale: these tokens often introduce clauses that change or qualify the meaning of the left span, producing high contradiction in the measured label.

rules.surface_condition: markers immediately before parenthetical/acronym tokens (right-side tokens that are short uppercase-style acronyms or identifier codes)
rules.proposed_rule: Scoring rule (downgrade parenthetical/acronym continuation): If the token immediately after the marker is a short acronym/identifier token that commonly appears inside parentheses or as an inline code (examples in data: isil, kv62, nsa), lower the predicted score to a modest band (suggested target band: 10–40). Rationale: such tokens usually continue or disambiguate the named entity and the left-alone translation can be contradicted or altered by the parenthetical expansion.

tie_fix: Ties arise when multiple markers match the same surface-rule bucket; add a deterministic tiny offset (e.g., +index*0.01) when converting buckets to integers so identical-rule matches do not produce exact equal integers.
summary: The model over-ranks cuts that sit immediately before clause-introducing tokens (because/causing/due) or before parenthetical/acronym tokens (ISIL, KV62, NSA). Both patterns recur and are associated with high contradiction; explicitly lowering scores for those right-first tokens will push the keeper decision away from boundaries that the remainder tends to overturn. The proposed rules are conservative, token-anchored downgrades (narrow target bands) to avoid wide collateral demotion of unrelated safe cuts.
